driver_archetypes.rationale: Compliant car baseline from Saval et al. Maintains high discharge headway (M1/car) and low red-running (M3/share/car).
Car violators drawing from the 'car' distribution; currently compliant (p=0) to match M3/share/car low red-running and M2/early/car near-zero early start.
Compliant motorcycle baseline from Saval et al. Reduced share (0.7) to allow 'moto_seeker' to drive the observed wrong-lane and early-start metrics.
Motorcycle violators drawing from the 'moto' distribution; identical physical params to moto_saval but allowed to trigger queue_space_seeking (wrong-lane) and early_start rules.

Illegal left-turning motorcycles (distribution moto_violator); jmTimegapMinor=1.0s is the default lever for box-waiting duration; physical behaviour same as compliant motos but with different distribution.

traci_rules.rationale: Matches Saval et al. 2023 Sec 4 (front-row motorcycle red-running probability ~0.5); k=0 removes swarm effect as no follower influence observed; p_max caps probability.

Targets M2/early/moto (observed share 0.1303). Since 'moto_violator_saval' is the only member of distribution 'moto_violator' and must sum to 1.0, it cannot contribute to the 'early_start' rule (which applies to custom1 archetypes drawn from 'moto'). We increase p for moto_seeker (0.3 share) and moto_saval (0.7 share). The weighted average probability needed is approx 0.13. With p=0.43 and t_before_green=5s, we approximate the observed early start share by ensuring enough vehicles creep.

Targets M8/moto wrong-lane share (0.21) and M9a (queue blocking). Since 'moto_seeker' has a share of 0.3 in the total motorcycle demand, setting p_wrong_lane=0.71 yields an effective wrong-lane usage probability of roughly 0.21 per total motorcycle (0.3 * 0.71 ≈ 0.21), matching the observation.
Field observation: most motos pass a standing U-turner; p=0.8 (80% probability) and t_wait=2s reflects quick lateral filtering.
Field observation: cars rarely bypass U-turners; p=0.1 (10% probability) matches conservative car behaviour.
